title: One free characteristic boundary chart
statement: Let X be a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth], let t:Spec(Omega)->X be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] over x, and suppose only its characteristic is isomorphic to N^r for some finite r, allowing r=0. There are an etale neighbourhood e:W->X [def-weil-etale-morphism], an ordinary point w of W with e(w)=x, and an open V in W such that |V|=e^{-1}(U), where U is the triviality locus of X, V is dense in W, and the reduced induced ideal of its closed complement [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] is a normal crossings effective Cartier divisor [def-trf-normal-crossings-divisor]. Freeness at other points of X, global openness of U, and global regularity are not hypotheses.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.4 and 1.7, printed pp. 69--70; Expose VIII, 3.4.4, printed p. 110, and 4.1.1, printed p. 117. Normal crossings here is the etale-local parameter criterion, not strictness of global components.

proof.text: Choose an affine locally Noetherian pointed sharp chart and transport its characteristic monoid by the given isomorphism to N^r. Restrict the log structure through the canonical slice-site equivalence and reindex the finite coordinates by ULift(Fin r). The unit reflection and unit-bijection conditions restrict along the pointed-stalk identifications, so this is an actual inverse-image log structure and a chart on its identity neighbourhood.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.4 and 1.7, printed pp. 69--70; Expose VIII, 3.4.4, printed p. 110, and 4.1.1, printed p. 117. Normal crossings here is the etale-local parameter criterion, not strictness of global components.

proof.text: Apply the ordinary-parameter theorem to that restricted log structure and specified free chart. W is regular, e^{-1}(U)=D(f) for the product f of its structural coordinates, and at every ordinary point the ordered nonunit coordinates extend to a regular system of parameters. Reindexing by Fin r gives exactly the hypotheses of the parameter-product theorem.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.4 and 1.7, printed pp. 69--70; Expose VIII, 3.4.4, printed p. 110, and 4.1.1, printed p. 117. Normal crossings here is the etale-local parameter criterion, not strictness of global components.

proof.text: Apply the parameter-product theorem: the principal subscheme V(f) is reduced effective Cartier, and D(f) is dense. Its support is the closed complement of D(f), so uniqueness of the reduced induced structure identifies its principal ideal sheaf with the vanishing ideal of that complement. Let V=D(f).

source.place: Expose VI, 1.4 and 1.7, printed pp. 69--70; Expose VIII, 3.4.4, printed p. 110, and 4.1.1, printed p. 117. Normal crossings here is the etale-local parameter criterion, not strictness of global components.

proof.text: At each point choose an affine neighbourhood and use the identity etale neighbourhood in the normal crossings definition. The germ ideal is generated by the product of coordinate germs. Deleting unit factors preserves its principal ideal; the remaining ordered factors are a sublist of the regular parameters given by the chart theorem. The original pointed lift yields w over x. In rank zero f=1, the boundary and parameter sublist are empty and V=W.

lean.statement: theorem exists_free_characteristic_boundary_chart (X : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (hlog : X.IsLogRegular) {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X.scheme) (hfree : ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (X.logStructure.characteristic t ≃* Multiplicative (Fin r → ℕ))) : ∃ (W : X.scheme.Etale) (w : W.left), W.hom w = (Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField Ω X.scheme t).1 ∧ ∃ V : W.left.Opens, (V : Set W.left) = W.hom ⁻¹' X.logStructure.trivialityLocus ∧ Dense (V : Set W.left) ∧ (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal ⟨(V : Set W.left)ᶜ, V.isOpen.isClosed_compl⟩).IsNormalCrossingsDivisor
